copy.name: How to play hangman
copy.blurb: Rules, best letters and word patterns.
copy.title: How to play hangman and guess the word
copy.lead: Hangman is a word-guessing game: the word is shown as blanks and you guess one letter at a time before six wrong guesses finish the drawing. You will learn the rules, which letters to try first, and how to read the pattern of a half-solved word.
copy.result: A way to guess that finds most words in three or four misses, and a way to pick words that are hard to guess.
copy.note: The best letters differ by list. The tips below are for the English list; the Spanish list starts with A, O, E, I and the Indonesian list with A, N, E, R.
copy.s1b: Choose the word language and a category, or leave All categories. The word appears as one blank per letter; spaces and hyphens are shown.
copy.s2b: Guess a letter by tapping it or typing it. A right letter fills every blank it belongs in. A wrong letter adds a part to the figure: head, body, two arms, two legs. The sixth wrong guess ends the game.
copy.s3b: Try the letters found in the most words first. In this game's English list E is in 61 % of the words, then A, R, N, O and I. Two or three vowels early show the shape of the word quickly.
copy.s4b: Look at what the filled letters suggest: a word ending in _ _ G is often -ING, Q is almost always followed by U, and a double letter limits the choices. Use the category to narrow it down.
copy.s5t: Use a hint only when stuck
copy.s5b: Hint reveals one hidden letter but counts as a wrong guess. It is not offered on your last guess or for the final letter, so use it while you still have a few guesses left and no good idea.
copy.s6t: Pick a hard word for a friend
copy.s6b: Under Play with a friend, type a secret word. Short words with rare letters (J, Q, X, Z) and few repeated letters are hardest to guess, because common letters miss.
copy.diagram1: The board: blanks, wrong letters and the six parts of the figure.
copy.diagram2: Share of words in the game's English list that contain each letter: try the long bars first.

faq.q1: How many wrong guesses do you get in hangman?
faq.a1: Six in the usual game, one for each part of the figure: head, body, two arms and two legs. Some versions add a face, hands or feet for more chances.
faq.q2: What is the best first letter?
faq.a2: E: it is in 61 % of the words in this game's English list. After it, try A, R, N, O and I.
faq.q3: What are the hardest words in hangman?
faq.a3: Short words with uncommon letters, such as JINX, FJORD or QUIZ. Long words are easier because each guess has more chances to hit.
faq.q4: Do accents count in the Spanish list?
faq.a4: No. Guessing A also reveals Á, and U reveals Ü. Ñ has its own key.
faq.a5: Yes. It trains you to think about which letters a word can contain and in what order, and the category gives a hint of the meaning.

copy.name: Rock paper scissors rules
copy.blurb: What beats what, and how people play.
copy.title: Rock paper scissors: rules and how to win
copy.lead: Rock paper scissors is a hand game for two: both players show a hand sign at the same moment and one sign beats the other. You will learn the rules, how a best-of match works, the five-move Lizard Spock version, and the patterns people fall into.
copy.result: The full rules for both versions and a few habits to watch for when you play a person.
copy.note: Against a computer that throws at random no strategy helps: you win a third of the time over many rounds. The patterns below only work against people.
copy.s1t: Open Rock paper scissors on cv.cm
copy.s1b: Choose the rules and the match length. Tap a move, or press R, P or S on the keyboard.
copy.s2b: Rock crushes scissors, scissors cut paper, and paper covers rock. If both players show the same sign, the round is a draw.
copy.s3b: Best of 3 means the first player to win two rounds wins the match; best of 5 needs three wins. Draws do not count, so a match can last longer than its number.
copy.s4b: The five-move version adds lizard and Spock. Each move beats two others and loses to two: scissors decapitate lizard, lizard poisons Spock, Spock smashes scissors, Spock vaporizes rock, rock crushes lizard, lizard eats paper and paper disproves Spock. On the keyboard, L throws lizard and K throws Spock.
copy.s5b: People are bad at being random. Many repeat a sign after winning and switch after losing, often to the sign that would have beaten their last one. Many beginners also open with rock.
copy.s6b: The page lists your last rounds and counts each sign you threw. If one sign is far ahead, a person playing you could spot it too.
copy.diagram1: Each sign beats the next one around the circle.
copy.diagram2: Lizard Spock: every move beats two others and loses to two.

faq.q1: What beats what in rock paper scissors?
faq.a1: Rock beats scissors, scissors beat paper, and paper beats rock. The same sign on both sides is a draw.
faq.q2: What is the best first move?
faq.a2: Against a random opponent there is none. Against a beginner, paper does slightly better, because many beginners open with rock.
faq.q3: Is the computer here really random?
faq.a3: Yes. It draws its sign with your browser's cryptographic random number generator when you throw, and never sees your choice.
faq.q4: Where does the game come from?
faq.a4: Hand games like it go back centuries in East Asia. The rock, paper and scissors version spread from Japan, where it is called jan-ken, and became known around the world in the 20th century.
faq.a5: Sam Kass and Karen Bryla. They added two moves so that two players choose the same sign less often.

copy.name: How to calculate BAC
copy.title: How to calculate blood alcohol content (BAC)
copy.lead: Blood alcohol content (BAC) is how much alcohol is in your blood. You can estimate it from what you drank, your weight and the time that has passed with the Widmark formula. You will learn each part of the formula and what the result means, and why it is only an estimate.
copy.result: An estimate of your BAC now and how many hours until it falls to zero.
copy.note: This is an estimate for an average person, not a measurement. Food, health, medicines and how fast you drank all change the real level. Never use it to decide whether to drive.
copy.s1t: Open the BAC calculator on cv.cm
copy.s1b: Choose your sex and enter your body weight in kilograms or pounds. These set how far the alcohol is diluted in your body.
copy.s2t: Work out the grams of alcohol
copy.s2b: Multiply the drink size in mL by its alcohol % and by 0.789, the weight of 1 mL of alcohol. A 355 mL can of 5 % beer holds 355 × 0.05 × 0.789 = 14 g, one U.S. standard drink.
copy.s3b: Divide the grams by your weight in grams times a body water factor, 0.68 for men and 0.55 for women, and multiply by 100. Three such beers for a 70 kg man: 42 ÷ (70,000 × 0.68) × 100 = 0.088 %.
copy.s4b: The body clears about 0.015 % an hour, and nothing speeds it up: not coffee, water, a cold shower or sleep. Two hours after starting, the example is 0.088 − 0.030 = 0.058 %.
copy.s5b: Countries write the same value differently: 0.08 % equals 0.8 ‰ (grams per litre) and 80 mg per 100 mL. Many driving limits are 0.05 %, most U.S. states use 0.08 % (Utah 0.05 %), and some countries use 0.02–0.03 % or zero.
copy.s6b: Divide the BAC by 0.015 to get the hours left. The example needs almost four more hours. The calculator shows the time to 0.08, 0.05, 0.02 and zero.
copy.diagram1: The Widmark formula with a worked example.
copy.diagram2: BAC falls by about 0.015 % an hour after the peak.

faq.q1: How accurate is a BAC calculator?
faq.a1: It gives an average. Real levels can be well above or below it, depending on food, body build, health, medicines and how quickly you drank.
faq.q2: How many drinks can I have before driving?
faq.a2: No calculator can tell you that safely. Limits differ by country and some are zero, and impairment starts below the limit. If you have been drinking, do not drive.
faq.q3: Why do women reach a higher BAC from the same drinks?
faq.a3: On average a woman's body holds less water for the same weight, so the same alcohol is less diluted. The formula uses 0.55 instead of 0.68 for that.
faq.a4: Food in the stomach slows how fast alcohol is absorbed, so the peak is lower and later. It does not make the body clear alcohol faster.
faq.a5: A fixed amount of pure alcohol: 14 g in the U.S., 10 g in Australia, and 8 g (one unit) in the UK. A can of beer, a glass of wine and a shot are each close to one U.S. standard drink.

copy.name: How to calculate simple interest
copy.blurb: I = P × r × t with examples.
copy.title: How to calculate simple interest
copy.lead: Simple interest is paid only on the amount you first borrowed or saved, so it grows by the same amount every year. You will learn the formula, how to count months and days, how to work back to the principal, rate or time, and how it differs from compound interest.
copy.result: The interest and total for any principal, rate and time, and the missing value when you know the other three.
copy.note: Loans and savings that compound, such as most mortgages, credit cards and savings accounts, grow faster than this. Check which kind yours uses.
copy.s1t: Open the Simple interest calculator on cv.cm
copy.s1b: Choose what to find: the interest and total, or the principal, rate or time.
copy.s2b: Interest I = P × r × t: the principal times the yearly rate as a decimal times the time in years. 10,000 at 5 % for 3 years: 10,000 × 0.05 × 3 = 1,500.
copy.s3t: Turn the rate into a decimal
copy.s3b: Divide the percentage by 100: 5 % is 0.05 and 4.5 % is 0.045. The rate must be per year; a monthly rate times 12 gives the yearly rate.
copy.s4b: Divide months by 12 and days by 365. Some loans use a 360-day year, which gives a little more interest: 10,000 at 6 % for 90 days is 147.95 on 365 days but 150.00 on 360.
copy.s5b: Rearrange the formula: P = I ÷ (r × t), r = I ÷ (P × t) and t = I ÷ (P × r). Earning 300 on 5,000 at 4 % takes 300 ÷ (5,000 × 0.04) = 1.5 years.
copy.s6b: Add the interest to the principal for the total you repay or receive: 11,500 in the first example. Compounded yearly at the same rate it would be 11,576.25, and the gap grows every year. The table shows both.
copy.diagram1: The simple interest formula with an example.
copy.diagram2: Simple interest grows in equal steps; compound interest grows faster.

faq.q1: What is the simple interest formula?
faq.a1: I = P × r × t, where P is the principal, r the yearly rate as a decimal and t the time in years. The total is P + I.
faq.q2: How do I calculate simple interest per month?
faq.a2: Divide the yearly interest by 12. 10,000 at 6 % a year earns 600 a year, or 50 a month.
faq.q3: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
faq.a3: Simple interest is paid on the principal only. Compound interest is also paid on earlier interest, so it grows faster over time.
faq.q4: Why do some loans use a 360-day year?
faq.a4: It is an old banking convention that made calculations easier. Dividing the days by 360 instead of 365 makes the interest about 1.4 % higher.
faq.a5: Many car loans and short personal loans, bond coupons and some savings certificates. Mortgages, credit cards and savings accounts usually compound.
